correctness.rationale: Positive increasing P gives bounded expansive weights; P(n+k)/P(k) has exact degree five in n, giving the strict sixth-difference identity, not the fifth. Cauchy-dual moments telescope to P(0)/P(n). Subtracting the two quadratic Laplace resolvents, then convolving with e^(−at), yields the signed density in RESULT.md; its logarithmic-coordinate absolute value is bounded by a constant times (1+t)e^(−min(a,b)t). The finite signed density is uniquely determined by its Hausdorff moments, so its continuous interior sign is decisive. With y=ct the integrand factors as (2/3)sin(y/2)(1−cos(y/2))(4cos(y/2)+1), with signs +,−,+,− over one period; hence minima only at 0, 2π, 4π. At 2π the sign is that of 5−(8λ²+13)e^(−2πλ), immediately excluding λ≤0. For positive λ the full-period integral is strictly positive, with each new period a positive accumulated offset plus a rescaled first period. The log-equation derivative is positive since 16λ/(8λ²+13)≤√(8/13). At equality the only interior vanishing point is y=2π (the derivative has a strict sign change and F''(2π)=2e^(−2πλ)); hence x=e^(−2π/c). The independent numerical replay /tmp/opencode/frozen_math_samples_a91d.py gives λ*=0.1543920340043247835587; check.py was inspected, not executed. Its printed period and recurrence counts overstate the loops (four positive-λ period evaluations and 84 recurrence comparisons); the diagnostics are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The first noninteger ratio of two positive integral frequencies in lowest terms is a natural test outside the equal-real-part integer resonance classification. The result exactly resolves when finite positive damping restores an entire representing measure, and identifies the singular boundary location. It is a reusable nonvertical benchmark for positivity tests with competing frequencies, without a claim to classify other ratios.
